transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (ApexFlow), Ethan Brown (ApexFlow), Sara Lopez (ApexFlow)

Summary:
Short scoping call to walk through Redwood SDK integration (Python + TS) for a POC, discuss auth flows, sandbox -> prod guardrails, and initial benchmarking plan. Focus on private deployment needs and KMS key management.

Topics:
- SDK quickstart and env variables
- Auth patterns (API keys vs SSO vs workload identity)
- VPC / private deployment constraints and audit logs
- Perf baseline plan and what telemetry we need
- Next steps for POC kickoff and responsibilities

Transcript (imperfect auto-transcript, timestamps every ~30-60s):
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. i'm maya, i'm the account lead, daniel is our solutions engineer, we'll run through a quickstart and then map that to your POC needs.
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks maya, excited. we've got about 45–60 minutes. main thing is we want to understand how the SDK plugs into our microservice stack and also the auth story for private data.
[00:30] Daniel Ortiz: cool, high-level first — Redwood SDK provides python and typescript clients that wrap the http api, support streaming, embeddings, and there's a small console utility for env bootstrapping. i'll share the repo link at the end.
[00:47] Ethan Brown: couple quick context points: we run k8s on aws, want to keep traffic in our VPC, and use our own KMS for key wrapping. latency target is p95 < 150ms for short prompts, and cost is a factor; we expect bursts.
[01:05] Daniel Ortiz: understood. two options: hosted API which is fastest to start, and private deployment (VPC or on-prem). private gives you control over KMS and ingress, but adds ops — we'll scope that for the POC.
[01:22] Sara Lopez: security question — are audit logs and SSO integrations available out of the box? we need SAML/SCIM, RBAC, and logs shipped to our SIEM.
[01:34] Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles in the console, and audit logs can forward to your syslog or cloud logging. dan can show the config snippets.
[01:46] Daniel Ortiz: (screen share) okay opening the quickstart repo — there's a python folder with a simple flask example and a typescript node example using express. env variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (sandbox|prod), REDWOOD_REGION, and optional REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID for private deployments.
[02:10] (crosstalk)
[02:14] Priya Nair: quick q: for KMS, do we have to use provider-managed keys or can we supply our own CMKs?
[02:20] Daniel Ortiz: you can supply your CMK — in private deployments we support bringing your own KMS/HSM provider; for hosted the key is in our KMS but you can envelope encrypt client-side. sometimes the transcript says "CMQ" but it's CMK.
[02:34] Ethan Brown: and network egress — how do we ensure egress stays within our VPC?
[02:38] Daniel Ortiz: for VPC private deployment we place inference nodes in your subnet, we use NAT rules per your security policy; for hosted, we have peering and private link options to route traffic through your cloud project.
[02:52] Sara Lopez: compliance — do you have SOC2 and iso? we need SOC2 type II and periodic penetration test reports.
[02:58] Maya Chen: yes, SOC2 type II available; we'll add the security pack link in the follow-up. dan, note to attach the compliance pack.
[03:08] Daniel Ortiz: noted. also one nuance: there is a behavior around prefix caching and KV cache — if you're doing very low-latency streaming, you might want caching off for the first pass. sometimes the transcript reads K-V cash which is fine but it's KV cache.
[03:28] Priya Nair: that's interesting, our prompts are fairly templated so prefix caching could help cost. but we need deterministic outputs for some workflows. can we pin model versions?
[03:38] Daniel Ortiz: yes, you can pin model versions in the route config and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to quantized variants if latency spikes.
[03:48] Ethan Brown: demo the auth flow in code pls — how do we rotate keys, and for CI pipelines we want ephemeral tokens.
[03:54] Daniel Ortiz: sure, i'll switch to the python example.
[03:58] [Screen share: python/quickstart/app.py]
[04:05] Daniel Ortiz: here's a snippet — from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"), env=os.getenv("REDWOOD_ENV")); resp = client.generate(prompt)... In CI we recommend workload-identity or short-lived token provider; we have a guide for GCP Workload Identity and AWS OIDC.
[04:27] Priya Nair: can you show the short-lived token flow for github actions?
[04:31] Daniel Ortiz: yeah, we provide a GH action that exchanges an OIDC token for a short-lived credential — that way you don't store a long-lived API key in secrets. it's in the repo under .github/actions/oidc-exchange.
[04:44] Maya Chen: note — we'll include the GH example in the repo we send.
[04:48] Ethan Brown: about metrics — what traces do you surface? we want per-route latency, token counts, user-id level aggregation for cost apportionment.
[04:58] Daniel Ortiz: console exposes token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, per-model, and per-route breakdowns. we also emit otel spans and request-level metadata you can forward to your tracing backend.
[05:12] Sara Lopez: do you retain raw user inputs? our legal team insists on short retention.
[05:17] Maya Chen: you can choose retention policy per project: zero retention, short-term, or full. for private deploy you can configure retention to zero and only store minimal logs. we'll capture that in the security doc.
[05:30] Priya Nair: for the POC we plan to run a week-long burst test with 100 qps sustained and spikes to 600 qps. what's the recommended deployment to simulate production?
[05:42] Daniel Ortiz: for that profile, we recommended dedicated pool with autoscale and burst capacity. for initial POC use hosted but with dedicated-like instance sizing in a sandbox — we'll provide a sizing worksheet.
[05:55] Ethan Brown: pricing question now — can you ballpark costs for dedicated vs hosted for 1M tokens/day?
[06:02] Maya Chen: i'll follow up with a pricing outline but generally dedicated reduces per-token cost but has a base reserved capacity fee. we'll send the dedicated sizing and cost model.
[06:14] Priya Nair: perfect. also curious about multi-region failover if a region has an outage — what's your fallback story?
[06:21] Daniel Ortiz: smart routing: we can route by region and have a fallback policy. we can failover to a compatible model variant in another region if latency is acceptable. for POCs we typically test simulated region failover.
[06:35] (silence, typing)
[06:40] Maya Chen: ok, quick run through of POC milestones — first: repo + sandbox access, second: baseline perf run, third: private deployment scoping if baseline looks good.
[06:52] Priya Nair: timeline for the POC? we want to kick off next week and have a run for two weeks.
[06:58] Maya Chen: sounds good; we'll prepare the sandbox and plan a SE deep-dive mid next week to go over infra specifics.
[07:06] Daniel Ortiz: i'll schedule a 90-minute deep-dive to review VPC peering, KMS setup, and sample infra-as-code snippets.
[07:15] Sara Lopez: i'll share our security checklist and the contact for compliance.
[07:19] Maya Chen: great, thanks. any other questions?
[07:24] Ethan Brown: one small thing — do you have a sample helm chart or k8s deployment for the client side? we prefer to deploy a sidecar for request shaping.
[07:31] Daniel Ortiz: yes, we have a lightweight sidecar example and helm chart in the repo under infra/helm. it's been used for request shaping and token-billing attribution.
[07:43] Priya Nair: ok that's helpful.
[07:46] Maya Chen: final recap: dan will send the quickstart repo and GH OIDC example; i'll send pricing and the Dedicated sizing worksheet; priya and sara will send prompt set and security checklist. then SE deep dive week of 5/26.
[08:03] (wrap-up, thanks)
